## eDNA data standards

**Two major eDNA data standards exist**

::::: {.columns .standards}

:::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.standard-card}
[1. MIxS]{.standard-name}

Minimum Information about any (x) Sequence — for raw sequences

[Used by]{.repo-label}\
[INSDC]{.repo .repo-group} [NCBI]{.repo} [ENA]{.repo} [DDBJ]{.repo}
:::
::::

:::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.standard-card .fragment .highlight-dwc}
[2. Darwin Core (DwC)]{.standard-name}

Community vocabulary for biodiversity data — species, location, date, basis of record

[Used by]{.repo-label}\
[OBIS]{.repo} [GBIF]{.repo} [ALA]{.repo}
:::
::::

:::::

**Developing landscape**

- Rapidly changing field
- For OBIS future directions include the DWC-DP and FAIReDNA terms

::: {.notes}
Raw sequences deposited in NCBI lack coordinates and dates — they cannot answer where or when a species was detected. OBIS, GBIF, and ALA now accept DNA-derived occurrences linked to space and time. DNA data requires special care: it is derived, depends on reference databases, and often produces many unknown sequences. The Darwin Core DNA extension preserves methodological context for future re-analysis.

INSDC is shown dashed because it is the umbrella body — NCBI, ENA and DDBJ are its three member archives, mirroring each other's records, not four separate places to deposit.

One click highlights the Darwin Core card, which is what the rest of the session is about; the click after that moves on.
:::
